metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (COBOL program PAYRUN.cbl) with a deployable entry point (JCL job PAYRUN.jcl executed on z/OS mainframe via CA-7 scheduler). Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: Batch processing system triggered by schedule (CA-7 biweekly), reads employee data, computes payroll, writes output file, and transfers via FTP. No synchronous API surface. Matches event-processor detection signals: batch processing patterns with no synchronous API.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Overall score 1.20 yields Not Ready band (< 1.5) but 11 High findings map to Remediation Required tier (2-11 High). The divergence arises because nearly all questions score 1, driving the overall score below 1.5, while the count-based classification caps Remediation Required at 2-11 High. Both signals confirm this system requires comprehensive modernization.

findings.title: Managed Compute
findings.description: All compute runs on IBM z/OS mainframe (COBOL batch via JCL). The only AWS presence is a single EC2 m4.large instance serving as a plaintext FTP file gateway. No managed container orchestration or serverless.
findings.gap: No managed compute services. Mainframe requires specialized skills and cannot scale elastically.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite batch processing in a modern language and deploy on AWS Batch, ECS/Fargate, or Lambda.

findings.title: Managed Databases
findings.description: Database is IBM DB2 for z/OS v10, self-managed on mainframe. The COBOL program reads from VSAM indexed files. No managed AWS database services in use.
findings.gap: All data storage is self-managed on mainframe with manual patching, no automated failover, and end-of-support engine.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL or RDS PostgreSQL using AWS SCT and DMS.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration
findings.description: Batch orchestration is entirely hardcoded in JCL (STEP010: run PAYRUN, STEP020: FTP). No managed workflow orchestration. Event-processor archetype expects managed orchestration for multi-step processing.
findings.gap: No dedicated orchestration service. JCL provides only primitive sequential execution with no retry logic or error handling.
findings.recommendation: Implement AWS Step Functions for batch workflow orchestration with retry logic and execution visibility.

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure. File-based I/O and plaintext FTP for data transfer. For event-processor archetype, absence of managed event sources is a significant gap.
findings.gap: No event-driven architecture. Data transfer relies on plaintext FTP rather than managed messaging services.
findings.recommendation: Replace FTP with managed messaging (SQS/EventBridge) or S3 event notifications. Use EventBridge Scheduler for job triggering.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: No VPC, security groups, or network segmentation. Plaintext FTP transmits PII (SSN, bank accounts) to hardcoded IP without encryption or isolation.
findings.gap: No network security configuration. Sensitive PII transmitted over plaintext FTP with no network isolation.
findings.recommendation: Deploy all workloads in VPC with private subnets, least-privilege security groups, and encrypted transfer (AWS Transfer Family).

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, or managed entry point. System is batch-only with outbound FTP as the only external communication.
findings.gap: No managed entry point for external communication.
findings.recommendation: Implement API Gateway or ALB with authentication and throttling when modernizing to expose API surface.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: No auto-scaling. Mainframe batch with statically allocated resources (REGION=0M). EC2 m4.large gateway has no scaling configuration.
findings.gap: All capacity statically provisioned. No ability to scale with workload changes.
findings.recommendation: Configure auto-scaling for compute (ECS/Fargate or AWS Batch) appropriate for batch workload patterns.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: No backup configuration found. GDG format provides basic output versioning but no comprehensive backup/recovery strategy.
findings.gap: No automated backup or recovery procedures for employee data or payroll outputs.
findings.recommendation: Enable automated backups with PITR for managed databases and cross-region replication for critical payroll data.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: No IaC exists. Zero IaC files found. All infrastructure is manually created and maintained.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage. All infrastructure changes are manual, non-reproducible, and undocumented.
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure in IaC (CDK or Terraform) starting with the modernized architecture.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. All deployments to mainframe are manual. No automated build, test, or deploy stages.
findings.gap: No automated quality gates. Manual process is error-prone with no reproducibility.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline (CodePipeline + CodeBuild or GitHub Actions) with automated build, test, and deploy stages.

findings.title: Programming Languages
findings.description: Primary language is COBOL (Enterprise COBOL 4.2) with JCL. COBOL has no AWS SDK, no cloud-native tooling, and scarce skills (original authors retired).
findings.gap: COBOL has no path to cloud-native development. No AWS SDK, no container compatibility, no modern frameworks.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite in a modern cloud-native language: Java 17+ (Spring Boot 3.x), Python 3.10+, or TypeScript (Node.js 18+).

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices
findings.description: Single COBOL program handles all payroll processing. No module boundaries, no service separation, pervasive shared state in WORKING-STORAGE.
findings.gap: Tightly-coupled monolith. Cannot independently scale, deploy, or evolve components.
findings.recommendation: During rewrite, decompose into bounded contexts: employee data, tax calculation, payment processing, reporting.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication
findings.description: Entirely file-based batch I/O with synchronous FTP transfer. No async patterns, no message queues. Anti-pattern for event-processor archetype which should use async event sources.
findings.gap: No async communication. File-based FTP creates tight coupling. Anti-pattern for event-processor archetype.
findings.recommendation: Replace file-based FTP with async patterns: SQS/SNS for results, S3 event notifications, EventBridge Scheduler for triggering.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling
findings.description: Batch job runs 5-7 hours with no checkpointing. Sequential processing of all employees with no resume capability. Failure requires full restart.
findings.gap: Long-running batch (5-7 hours) with no checkpointing or progress tracking. Sometimes overruns batch window.
findings.recommendation: Implement checkpoint/restart with AWS Step Functions Map state or AWS Batch array jobs for partitioned parallel processing.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: No API versioning. No API surface exists. Output file format (120-byte fixed-width) has no schema versioning.
findings.gap: No versioning strategy for any interface. Format changes are breaking for all downstream consumers.
findings.recommendation: Implement API versioning and schema versioning (Avro/Protobuf) for data exchange formats.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: All endpoints hard-coded. EC2 gateway IP (10.0.7.40) and dataset names (ACME.PAYROLL.*) hardcoded directly in JCL.
findings.gap: Hard-coded endpoints create deployment coupling. Cannot relocate services without source code changes.
findings.recommendation: Externalize endpoints into configuration. Use AWS Service Discovery or Parameter Store.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: All data stored on mainframe file systems — VSAM indexed files and GDG datasets. No cloud storage (S3). Data locked in mainframe-specific formats inaccessible to modern systems.
findings.gap: Data on mainframe file systems is inaccessible for modern workloads, analytics, or integration.
findings.recommendation: Migrate data to Amazon S3 with structured formats (Parquet/JSON) and schema definitions.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: Single COBOL program with inline file I/O. No formal data access layer or repository pattern. Business logic tightly coupled to file format.
findings.gap: No abstraction between business logic and data access. File format changes require changes throughout the program.
findings.recommendation: Implement repository/DAO pattern in the rewritten application to abstract data access behind interfaces.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
findings.description: IBM DB2 for z/OS v10 — end of support since April 2020 (5+ years past EOL). No security patches or vendor support available.
findings.gap: Database engine 5+ years past end-of-life with no upgrade or migration plan documented.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Aurora PostgreSQL or RDS PostgreSQL using AWS SCT for schema conversion and DMS for data migration.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest. Sensitive PII (SSN, bank accounts) stored unencrypted in VSAM files and transmitted via plaintext FTP.
findings.gap: Highly sensitive PII stored and transmitted without encryption. Critical compliance violation.
findings.recommendation: Encrypt all data at rest using customer-managed KMS keys. Enable storage encryption on databases and S3.

findings.title: API Authentication
findings.description: No API authentication. FTP uses hardcoded credentials (username: payroll, password in clear text) embedded in JCL.
findings.gap: No modern authentication mechanism. Plaintext credentials provide no security assurance.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2/JWT authentication on all endpoints. Replace FTP with SFTP or S3 presigned URLs.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: No identity provider integration. Authentication is a hardcoded username/password in JCL with no Cognito, Okta, or SAML/OIDC.
findings.gap: No centralized identity. Credentials are local, static, with no rotation or MFA.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with centralized IdP (Amazon Cognito or organizational IdP). Implement IAM roles for service auth.

findings.title: Secrets Management
findings.description: Plaintext credentials hardcoded in JCL: FTP username 'payroll' and password 'PayR0ll2003!' committed to Git repository.
findings.gap: Critical security vulnerability. Plaintext password in version-controlled source. No secrets management or rotation.
findings.recommendation: Immediately rotate exposed credentials. Store all secrets in AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: No patching strategy or vulnerability scanning. Source warns 'DO NOT RECOMPILE WITHOUT CONTACTING MAINFRAME TEAM' indicating no safe patching process.
findings.gap: No automated patching or vulnerability scanning. Fear of recompilation indicates no safe update path.
findings.recommendation: Implement SSM Patch Manager, vulnerability scanning (Inspector/Snyk), and hardened base images.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists, therefore no security scanning. No SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, or container scanning.
findings.gap: No security validation at any stage. Vulnerabilities cannot be detected before production.
findings.recommendation: Integrate SAST, dependency scanning, and container scanning with blocking gates in CI/CD pipeline.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No OpenTelemetry, no X-Ray. Batch job has no observability beyond mainframe job logs.
findings.gap: No tracing capability. Cannot trace data flow or diagnose failures within the batch run.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with OpenTelemetry or AWS X-Ray in the modernized application.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No monitoring artifacts. Batch window constraint (5-7 hours) is informal and not monitored.
findings.gap: No formal SLO definitions. Batch overruns discovered reactively.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for batch completion time, data accuracy, and transfer success rate with CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom business metrics. No tracking of employees processed, payroll amounts, error counts, or tax calculation accuracy.
findings.gap: No visibility into business outcomes without manual file inspection.
findings.recommendation: Publish business metrics: employees processed, payroll disbursed, FICA calculations, error counts via CloudWatch.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection. Failures discovered manually.
findings.gap: No automated alerting. Failures and data quality issues discovered reactively.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms for batch completion, processing duration, and record count anomalies.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: No automated tests. README states changes validated in shared QA region only. Source warns against recompilation.
findings.gap: Zero automated test coverage. Changes carry high regression risk.
findings.recommendation: Implement comprehensive test suites in the rewritten application: unit, integration, and output comparison tests.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership. No CODEOWNERS, no dashboards, no alarms with named owners. Original authors retired.
findings.gap: No observability ownership or monitoring responsibility defined.
findings.recommendation: Establish per-service dashboards, named alarm owners, CODEOWNERS, and on-call responsibilities.

decomposition_strategy.recommended_approach: Conditional / Adaptive (parallel build with phased cutover)
decomposition_strategy.rationale: COBOL mainframe with no module boundaries, no API surface, and no modern tooling cannot be incrementally strangled. Parallel rewrite with output comparison is the only viable path.

Containerize and deploy on ECS/Fargate with managed database
Parallel run comparing outputs for correctness
